summary: no-reply mailbox bounce alerts tagged 'spam-suspect' causing invoice delivery failures
description: The internal no-reply mailbox (no-reply_redwood@redwood.ai) is producing intermittent bounce alerts flagged as 'spam-suspect'. Finance reported five customers in the last 48 hours who did not receive invoice emails. Suspect causes: DKIM/SPF misconfig, Mailgun (or other ESP) routing, domain reputation, or a new suppression list entry. Requesting: 1) verify SPF/DKIM/DMARC for redwood.ai and subdomains; 2) check ESP logs for bounces/suppression and removal if erroneous; 3) inspect any recent changes to mailing templates or volume spikes; 4) whitelist no-reply_redwood where safe and notify Finance of temporary mitigation; 5) document root cause and remediation steps.
comments: 2025-11-12 Alex Kim: Assigned and started triage. Pulling ESP logs now; will check suppression list and recent template sends.
2025-11-12 Samantha Ortiz: Finance provided list of impacted accounts in the ticket attachment (see link in Drive). Please prioritize as invoices are time-sensitive.

2025-11-13 Alex Kim: ESP shows several 550 5.7.1 'spam-suspect' bounces to a subset of recipients. SPF/DKIM records look valid on quick check; requesting DNS TTLs and any recent DNS changes from infra.
2025-11-14 Priya Singh: Confirmed no DNS changes in the last 60 days. Suggest checking ESP suppression export and raising a support case with provider if suppression appears automated.

2025-11-15 Alex Kim: Removed two erroneous suppression entries and requeued 3 invoices; monitoring deliverability. Follow-up: open ticket with ESP support to confirm why these addresses were added to suppression list.
2025-11-15 Samantha Ortiz: Thanks — Finance confirmed two customers received re-sent invoices. Will track remaining follow-ups in this ticket.
